statement: The watcher reads a closed list of the Depository's events, checked against the deployed ABI: an event it does not know, a log of another address or a log of the wrong shape refuses the delivery and never reads as nothing.
source: consolidation-plan.md D9 (no silent refusals); lessons.md (a check that lives only in a CLI looks gated but is not)

layers.arrival: n/a: the watcher is Host code that reads a node; the Arrival specs take J events as given
layers.quint: n/a: which kinds of event are read is R-WATCH-READS-ALL (QUESTIONS R7); a closed list that refuses an unknown event is the Host's, which the Quint model does not have
layers.contract: n/a: no contract code takes part; the watcher reads the deployed Depository's events
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-WATCH-CLOSED a topic that is not lowercase bytes32 is a fault, not an event of Entities nobody hosts
R-WATCH-CLOSED a topic more than the event has is a fault, for each of the four events
R-WATCH-CLOSED data of the wrong length is a fault for a counter and a finalize, a word more or fewer
R-WATCH-CLOSED a dispute start shorter than its slots is a fault, as is half a word
R-WATCH-CLOSED an address is exactly twenty bytes
R-WATCH-CLOSED every event of the deployed Depository is read or named as ignored, and none is both
R-WATCH-CLOSED the topic 0 of each listed signature is the one the ABI computes
R-WATCH-CLOSED every log of the real lifecycle decodes: the four events are read, the rest are ignored
R-WATCH-CLOSED an event the Depository has never emitted is a fault, not a miss
R-WATCH-CLOSED a log of another address is a fault: the node is asked for the Depository's logs
R-WATCH-CLOSED an event the watcher does not know is a fault of the whole delivery and moves no cursor
